children: Russia's gross domestic product grew by 0.6% year-on-year in July after a revised 1.7% growth in June, the economy ministry's preliminary data showed on Wednesday.
In the first seven months of the year, the Russian economy grew by 0.6%, the data showed. The ministry had previously estimated June growth at 1.1%.
In May the economy ministry sharply downgraded its macroeconomic forecasts for 2026–2029 after more than four years of war in Ukraine. It cut its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.4% from 1.3%.
Economy minister Maxim Reshetnikov said on Wednesday that the ministry had slightly raised 2026 GDP growth forecast to 0.6%.
The central bank suggested that the economy might not grow at all this year, cutting its growth forecast to between zero and 1%.
